title: pip install, zero servers
description: Milvus Lite installs with `pip install pymilvus` and runs with a local URI — no Docker, no cluster, no server process. A Jupyter notebook can have a real vector database in two lines. It is the fastest path from embeddings to searchable vectors.

title: The milvus.db file
description: All data lives in a single milvus.db file (SQLite-based metadata + vector storage), so backup is a file copy and projects stay portable. The file can be checked into project storage or shipped with a demo. Local-first means the database is a file.

title: MilvusClient: the simple API
description: MilvusClient offers create_collection, insert, search, query, and delete without managing connections or partitions. It is the recommended API for Lite and small projects. Simple API, same engine semantics as full Milvus.

demo.program:
print('client = MilvusClient("./milvus.db")')
print('create_collection / insert / search / query')
demo.expected_output:
client = MilvusClient("./milvus.db")
create_collection / insert / search / query

title: Collections and schemas
description: Collections define fields: an id primary key, a vector field with dimension, and scalar fields for metadata. Schemas are declared up front so queries can filter on metadata later. Schema-first keeps retrieval precise.

title: Vector indexes: HNSW, IVF_FLAT
description: Lite supports HNSW (fast approximate search, more memory) and IVF_FLAT (balanced) index types, chosen per collection. Index choice trades recall against speed and RAM. Defaults are sensible; tuning comes later.

demo.program:
idx={'HNSW':'fast, more RAM','IVF_FLAT':'balanced'}
for k,v in idx.items(): print(k,'->',v)
demo.expected_output:
HNSW -> fast, more RAM
IVF_FLAT -> balanced

title: Distance metrics
description: Collections pick a metric: COSINE, L2, or IP (inner product), which must match how the embedding model was trained to be used. Wrong metric silently degrades results. Metric choice is a correctness issue, not a preference.

demo.program: print('metric must match the embedding model: COSINE/L2/IP')
demo.expected_output: metric must match the embedding model: COSINE/L2/IP

title: Filtered search
description: Search accepts a filter expression on scalar fields ('category == "sci-fi"'), combining vector similarity with metadata constraints. Filtered search is how RAG stays on-topic in multi-tenant data. Expressions use a simple SQL-like syntax.

title: Insert and upsert
description: insert() adds vectors with ids; upsert semantics come from inserting with existing ids in newer versions. Batch inserts in the thousands for throughput. IDs are the handle for updates and deletes.

title: Delete by expression
description: delete() removes vectors matching a filter expression, so stale documents leave the index cleanly. RAG pipelines delete by source file when documents update. Clean deletes keep retrieval honest.

title: Query (non-vector) lookups
description: query() fetches rows by filter without a vector, useful for metadata inspection and debugging what is actually in the collection. Debugging retrieval starts with querying what got stored. The same filter syntax applies.

title: Partition-free simplicity
description: Lite skips partitions and multi-tenancy features of full Milvus, which is exactly why it stays simple: one file, one API, no ops. When you need partitions and RBAC, you have outgrown Lite by design. Simplicity is the feature.

title: Embedding dimension discipline
description: The collection's dim must equal the embedding model's output dimension (384, 768, 1536...); mismatches error at insert. Recording the model name + dim in the collection description prevents mystery errors months later. Discipline at creation saves debugging.

demo.program: print('dim must equal model output dim; record model name')

title: Backup = copy the file
description: Because everything is one file, backups are cp milvus.db, versioning is file copies with dates, and sharing a dataset is sending the file. Operational simplicity is Lite's superpower for small projects. No backup tooling to learn.
